# Bug-Hunter Findings Ledger

Append-only log of findings from prior bug-hunter runs. Check this before starting a new sweep so you don't re-spend budget rediscovering the same bug. Update an entry's `Fix Status` in place when it changes — don't delete history, mark it.

Format: one entry per confirmed finding. `Fix Status: unfixed | fix applied, untested | fixed (test run + date)`.

---

### [Medium] PEP 735 Dependency Groups declared supported in spec, entirely unimplemented in code
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-03 sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:183-256` (`iter_dependencies`), `:258-343` (`update_dependency_spec`); spec: `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md:14`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Root Cause**: The Python engine spec lists PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`) as one of 5 core PEPs supported. `python.rs` only reads/writes `[project].dependencies` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` — no code anywhere references `dependency-groups`.
- **Failing Scenario**: A `pyproject.toml` with `[dependency-groups] test = ["pytest>=7.0"]` pinning an in-workspace sibling — a cascade-triggering bump never rewrites the entry, invisible to cascade/validate/version alike.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed — spec-correction/spec-completion pass dispatched 2026-08-03, code fix not yet started, pending that pass landing.

### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.
- **Fix**: `fetch_all_tags` (new) tries gix first, falls through (not `?`) to one `runner.run("git", &["tag","--list"], root)` call when unavailable — mirroring `changed.rs`'s existing pattern exactly, so no new design was invented. Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. Also added a call-counting test proving the N→1 batching.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `Version::deserialize` was hardcoded to `VersionGrammar::SemVer`, silently broken for PEP-440-only strings
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — the earlier deferral was revisited with real investigation, not just implemented blind
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Investigation**: grepped every real serde-deserialization call site for a `Version`-bearing type; found exactly one with no available grammar signal — `commands/tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` ingestion (reads a plan file/stdin from a potentially separate process/CI step, no sibling ecosystem field). Confirmed no PEP-440 `Version` reaches that path *today* (`plan_publish` has no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch yet), but PyPI/PEP 440 is a fully live, non-stub ecosystem elsewhere in the codebase (manifest parsing, bump logic, and the publish-client classifier are all already implemented) — so this was going to silently break the moment that wiring gap closed.
- **Fix**: `Version::deserialize` now tries `SemVer` first (strictest/most unambiguous), falls back to `Pep440` only if that fails — mirroring `VersionReq::deserialize`'s existing multi-grammar pattern. Residual ambiguity (a string valid under both grammars always resolves to SemVer) is documented directly on the impl and pinned by a test, matching the same accepted tradeoff `VersionReq` already carries.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `cargo.rs` silently dropped BOM on write despite a comment claiming it was handled
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback (same class as the earlier CST-fidelity fixes; this instance was missed because a code comment incorrectly claimed `toml_edit` handled it internally — that claim was true for the read path, false for the write path)
- **Root Cause**: `CargoToml::open` stripped the BOM before parsing but never recorded that fact; `persist()` wrote `self.document.to_string()` with no BOM restoration.
- **Fix**: Added `has_bom: bool`, populated on open, prepended back on `persist()` — mirrors `python.rs`'s existing pattern. Note: `WorkspaceCargoResolver`'s separate load/persist path was NOT covered by this fix and may have the same latent gap for a workspace-root `Cargo.toml` with a BOM — flagged, not verified either way.
- **Fix Status**: fixed (for `CargoToml` directly; `WorkspaceCargoResolver` unverified).

### [High→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam didn't route a missing-binary host-abort through its own promised `Result` — affected both `execute_extension` and `initialize_extension`
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Crash-Safety (falsifies the crate's own "never panics, every failure caught into the report" claim)
- **Root Cause**: When the target program (`moon`/`git`) can't be resolved, `warpgate` 0.30.5's host-side `exec_command` closure returns `Err` from *native* code — Extism aborts the entire plugin call rather than routing it back into the guest as a value the guest's own `Result` handling can see. `MoonCommandRunner::run`'s `Err(e) => classify_host_failure(...)` branch never ran; the whole host call failed instead.
- **Fix**: Pre-check existence via `warpgate_pdk::command_exists` (shells to `which`, not the target program, so a missing program yields an ordinary `false`) before calling `exec`, turning it into the clean `CommandError::NotFound` the method already promised.
- **Fix Status**: fixed. Found only because the new black-box failure-path tests (dispatched to close a coverage gap) immediately falsified the "never panics" claim on first write — exactly the kind of bug happy-path-only testing had been hiding.

### [High→fixed] `callisto add --dry-run` didn't apply `--dry-run` at all — wrote to disk anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (live-tested pre- and post-fix against the built CLI, both text and JSON output formats)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs`
- **Classification**: Unchecked Flag (same class as the original, already-fixed `version --dry-run` bug — recurred in a sibling command)
- **Fix**: computes and reports the would-be changeset content/path (both output formats) without calling `atomic_write`/`create_dir_all` when `global.dry_run` is set.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `callisto publish`'s output couldn't distinguish "computed a plan" from "actually published packages"
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `callisto_model::report::PublishReport`
- **Classification**: UX / Missing Feature
- **Fix**: new `PublishReport` type (following the codebase's existing `Plan`-vs-`Report` naming convention) carries per-package `PublishAttempt`/outcome; `PublishOrchestrator::execute` now returns it instead of `()`; the CLI's real (non-dry-run) path prints/returns it instead of re-rendering the input plan.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `CliError::Io`/`CliError::Registry` lacked `help()` text, inconsistent with `NotATty`'s pattern
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`
- **Fix**: `Io` converted to a struct variant carrying the failing path (with a manual `From<std::io::Error>` preserving `?`-ergonomics at call sites with no natural path), both variants now have actionable `help()` text. Verified with a real before/after repro (`callisto tag --plan /nonexistent/plan.json`).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Critical→fixed] `commands/tag.rs`'s `create_tags_with_options` hard-crashed on wasm — same bug class as the original tags.rs crash, not actually fixed everywhere
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (found via exhaustive call-site audit of `GitRepository::discover` prompted by finding the first instance in `tags.rs`)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs`
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap (same class as the already-fixed `tags.rs` bug)
- **Fix**: gix-discovered once at the top of the function; new `tag_exists` (read, gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback, mirrors `tags.rs`) and mutating fallbacks for `create_tag` (`git tag -a`, annotated, no-force) and `create_floating_major` (`git tag -f`, matching gix's exact current semantics) — but for the mutating paths, a real gix failure on a real repo is NOT masked by retrying through the shell (fallback only fires when gix was never discovered at all, not on a genuine gix error).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `callisto-conventional`'s `fetch_commits` discarded its `CommandRunner` param — silently dropped conventional-commit inference on wasm
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter
- **Fix**: gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback (mirroring `tags.rs`), new `fetch_commits_via_command_runner` shelling `git log --no-merges --format=\x1e%H\x1f%B <range> [-- <pathspecs>]` (RS/US control-char field separators, immune to misparsing multi-line commit messages; avoided `-z`/NUL-termination since it needs git ≥2.34, above this repo's declared `>=2.20` floor). A malformed/unparseable line now returns `ConventionalError::MalformedGitLogOutput` (a previously-dead-code variant) instead of silently dropping the commit.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `aggregate.rs`'s own `resolve_since` had no `CommandRunner` fallback either — silently degraded to unbounded full-history walk on wasm
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: same gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <tag>^{commit}`), preserving the existing invariant that a real gix `Ok` result (even `Ok(None)`) is authoritative and the `CommandRunner` is never touched when gix is actually available.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] Two independently-reinvented `PoisonedRunner` test doubles, near-identical
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` and `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`, now `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`
- **Classification**: Maintainability / Duplication
- **Fix**: `PoisonedRunner`/`run_git`/`init_repo` consolidated into `callisto-fixtures` (already a workspace dev-dependency), both call sites now import the shared version. `FakeGitTagRunner`/`ScriptedRunner` deliberately left alone — genuinely different test-double shapes, not the same duplication class.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `gix_wasi_spike.rs`'s pinned dev-dependencies were still consuming `cargo-deny` audit budget for a proven-NO-GO path
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-moon/examples/gix_wasi_spike.rs`
- **Classification**: Maintainability / Dead code
- **Fix**: spike file and its 12 spike-only pinned `gix-*` dev-dependencies removed; `cargo tree -i gix-odb` confirms only `callisto-vcs`'s real `gix` dependency remains in the tree. The finding itself stays fully documented in this ledger; `runner.rs`'s in-repo pointer updated to reference this ledger instead of the deleted file.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `apply_version_plan` silently discarded git staging failures, then reported success anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: both `git add`/`git rm --cached` call sites now propagate spawn errors via `?` and explicitly check `output.success()`, returning `Err(GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed{..}))` on failure instead of silently reporting `staged` as populated. Design decision (documented): fatal error, not a nuanced partial-success report — grepped all consumers of `ApplyOutcome.staged` and found none currently branch on it, so a hard error is strictly safer with no behavioral cost.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium] Per-package git-repo discovery + revwalk in severity inference — O(N_packages × C_commits) instead of O(C_commits)
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, performance sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:183-228`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:53-74`, `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs:22-31`
- **Classification**: Architectural / Algorithmic complexity
- **Root Cause**: `aggregate()` reuses a single `GitRepository` for `resolve_since`, but severity inference is separate — for every package, `fetch_commits` re-discovers the repo and runs its own independent revwalk + tree-diff from HEAD to that package's `since` bound. Most packages share largely the same commit window, so the tree-diff work over the shared range repeats once per package instead of once total.
- **Failing Scenario**: 150-package monorepo, most untagged in the last 40 commits — `aggregate()` triggers 150 separate `gix::discover` calls and 150 independent tree-diff walks over an overlapping range, instead of one HEAD walk bucketing each commit's touched paths against all pathspecs at once.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed, not yet dispatched. Note: with the `GitDataSource`/`GitAccess` abstraction now in place (see below), `resolve_since` and `fetch_commits` both go through a shared, single-discovery `GitAccess` instance per `aggregate()` call already — this finding is specifically about the per-package *revwalk/tree-diff* work still repeating, not repo re-discovery (that part is already fixed as a byproduct of the trait consolidation).

### [Low-Medium→fixed] `ManifestWalkResolver::build` deep-cloned the entire graph just to run the moon-declared-edges crosscheck

### [Critical→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam is a native-process stub — gix-in-WASM spike ruled out as a fix, host-exec bridge landed
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, including real black-box `.wasm` sandbox tests)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Crash-Safety / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: Implemented `CommandRunner` via `std::process::Command::new(program).output()`, which cannot function under WASI sandboxing (WASM guests can't spawn processes). A dedicated spike investigated whether gitoxide's low-level crates could instead read the repo natively from inside the guest (moon does grant a real WASI preopen at `/workspace`) — **NO-GO**: `gix-odb`/`gix-pack`/`gix-index` all read object/index content via `memmap2::Mmap` unconditionally; `memmap2` has no `wasm32-wasip1` backend and its stub returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` at runtime. Ref *names* resolve (loose refs use plain `std::fs`), but no object content is readable — confirmed via a real wasmtime run against a real fixture repo, not just static analysis.
- **Fix**: `MoonCommandRunner` now bridges through `warpgate_pdk::exec` (the real `#[host_fn] exec_command` binding) on the `pdk` (wasm) build, keeping the original `std::process::Command` path only for native (non-wasm) builds. Verified with genuine black-box coverage: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` builds the actual `.wasm`, loads it into a real wasmtime-backed Extism sandbox via `moon_pdk_test_utils`, and drives real `register_extension`/`execute_extension` wire calls — not just a type-check.
- **Follow-on bug found and fixed during final verification**: the fix's `Cargo.toml` initially declared `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` unconditionally, which made `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` (native, macOS) also attempt a **native** cdylib build/link whenever the `pdk` feature was on, failing on extism-pdk's WASM-host-only import symbols (`_alloc`, `_input_length`, etc. — undefined for native linking). Fixed by removing `crate-type` from the manifest entirely and instead requesting `--crate-type cdylib` explicitly only where the wasm artifact is actually needed (`just wasm-check`, the test's self-bootstrap build) via `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib`.
- **Also found and fixed during final verification**: `moon_pdk_test_utils`'s test-only dependency chain (`warpgate` → `extism` host crate → `wasmtime 41.0.4`) carries several open RUSTSEC advisories (sandbox-escape/miscompile class) plus one unmaintained-crate warning, none of which ship in the production `.wasm` artifact (only the lightweight guest-side `warpgate_pdk` does, which is unaffected). Scoped, documented `[advisories] ignore` added to `deny.toml` for these specific IDs — flagged there as **unstable across consecutive runs** (the RustSec advisory-db itself appears to be actively updated mid-session), so this list may need to grow again on a future CI run.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

- **Classification**: Crash-Safety / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: Implemented `CommandRunner` via `std::process::Command::new(program).output()`, which cannot function under WASI sandboxing (WASM guests can't spawn processes). - **Fix**: `MoonCommandRunner` now bridges through `warpgate_pdk::exec` (the real `#[host_fn] exec_command` binding) on the `pdk` (wasm) build, keeping the original `std::process::Command` path only for native (non-wasm) builds. # Universal Rust Bug-Hunter Skill

## Goal

Find real bugs before they ship in any Rust repository (monorepos, CLI engines, libraries, polyglot WASM plugins): silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, data corruption, ordering staleness, crash-safety violations, and edge cases that break production.

This skill is **Rigid**: follow it exactly across any Rust workspace.

## The Law

> NO FINDING MARKED `CONFIRMED` WITHOUT AN END-TO-END TRACE. NO FIX MARKED DONE WITHOUT A TEST THAT FAILED BEFORE THE FIX AND PASSES AFTER, RUN IN THIS SESSION.

## Core Rules

- **Verify by Tracing**: Don't trust a comment, docstring, passing test, or a prior audit's "FIXED" label. Trace the code execution path yourself.
- **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: When executing multi-agent bug hunts, DO NOT partition subagents by directory or crate names. ALWAYS partition subagents by **Hazard Taxonomy** or **Code Smell Sweep** across the entire workspace.
- **Strict Invariants**: Prioritize data integrity, crash-safety, error propagation, and security bugs over style or refactoring.
- **Read-Only Investigation**: Investigate and report findings first. Do not mutate files unless explicitly requested to apply fixes.

---

## The 6 Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies

1. **Discarded Data & Unused CLI / Struct Parameters**: Leading-underscore parameters (`_opts`, `_config`), unused Clap CLI flags.
2. **Ordering, Mutability & Fixpoint Staleness**: First-write-wins vs max-value-wins, graph solver loops missing re-enqueueing logic.
3. **Spec-vs-Code Compliance Drift**: Requirements in design docs/specs missing enforcement logic in functions.
4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.

---

## The 6 Architectural Code Smells & Ripgrep Sweeps

1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.
3. **Lossy Serde / CST Formatting Smell**: Replacing TOML/JSON nodes without preserving `.decor()` or line endings.
4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.
6. **Hardcoded Constant Dummy Smell**: Inserting placeholder strings (`"Release update"`, `"changeset.md"`) masking user metadata.

---

## 7 Shared Trait Centralization Framework

When auditing multi-crate workspaces, map recurring defects directly to 7 Centralized Rust Traits:
1. `PackageIdentityResolver`: Cross-ecosystem package matching and bare name resolution.
2. `VersionSpecRenderer`: Format & precision-preserving version requirement rendering.
3. `ChangesetStorage`: Crash-safe, transactional disk engine with parent directory fsync.
4. `CstManifestEditor`: CST format-preserving manifest modification (`toml_edit` and `serde_json`).
5. `GitVcsProvider`: Safe Git tags, shallow checkout handling, and bounded revwalk.
6. `CascadeSolver`: Fixpoint dependency graph solver & convergence tracking.
7. `ReportPresenter`: Unified text & JSON report renderer with rich `miette` diagnostic cards.

---

## Hazard-Taxonomy Multi-Agent Dispatch Matrix

| Agent Role | Scope | Objective |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`bug-hunter-scanner-rust`** | Taxonomies 1 & 4 | Scan workspace for unused CLI flags, discarded parameters, and silent `unwrap_or` defaults. |
| **`bug-hunter-adversary-rust`** | Taxonomies 2 & 3 | Trace execution paths end-to-end, disprove candidate signals, and check graph solver fixpoints and spec drift. |
| **`bug-hunter-remediator-rust`** | Taxonomies 5 & 6 | Audit boundary inputs, atomic write `.flush()`/`.sync_all()`, write failing regression tests (red), apply fixes. |
| **`bug-hunter-architect-rust`** | Smells 1-6 & Trait Centralization | Analyze recurring defect patterns, cluster code smells, and design lean Rust traits with formal contracts. |
| **`bug-hunter-mutator-rust`** | Mutation Testing & Coverage | Run `cargo-mutants`, find survived mutant branches, and write boundary unit tests ensuring assertions fail when code is mutated. |

---

Report each confirmed finding in this standard technical format:

```markdown
### [Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low] <Brief Vulnerability Title>

- **Status**: CONFIRMED (execution path fully traced, file:line cited) | PLAUSIBLE (strong signal, not fully traced)
- **Location**: `path/to/file.rs:L123-L135`
- **Classification**: [Discarded Parameter | Fixpoint Staleness | Spec Drift | Silent Fallback | Boundary Condition | I/O Safety]
- **Root Cause**: Concise explanation of the flaw in the current implementation logic.
- **Failing Scenario**: Concrete payload, CLI command, or input state that triggers the defect.
- **Verification Strategy**: A test that fails on current code and passes once fixed.
```

4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.
6. **Hardcoded Constant Dummy Smell**: Inserting placeholder strings (`"Release update"`, `"changeset.md"`) masking user metadata.

---

## 7 Shared Trait Centralization Framework

When auditing multi-crate workspaces, map recurring defects directly to 7 Centralized Rust Traits:
1. `PackageIdentityResolver`: Cross-ecosystem package matching and bare name resolution.
2. `VersionSpecRenderer`: Format & precision-preserving version requirement rendering.
3. `ChangesetStorage`: Crash-safe, transactional disk engine with parent directory fsync.
4. `CstManifestEditor`: CST format-preserving manifest modification (`toml_edit` and `serde_json`).
5. `GitVcsProvider`: Safe Git tags, shallow checkout handling, and bounded revwalk.
6. `CascadeSolver`: Fixpoint dependency graph solver & convergence tracking.
7. `ReportPresenter`: Unified text & JSON report renderer with rich `miette` diagnostic cards.

---

## Hazard-Taxonomy Multi-Agent Dispatch Matrix

| Agent Role | Scope | Objective |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`bug-hunter-scanner-rust`** | Taxonomies 1 & 4 | Scan workspace for unused CLI flags, discarded parameters, and silent `unwrap_or` defaults. |
| **`bug-hunter-adversary-rust`** | Taxonomies 2 & 3 | Trace execution paths end-to-end, disprove candidate signals, and check graph solver fixpoints and spec drift. |
| **`bug-hunter-remediator-rust`** | Taxonomies 5 & 6 | Audit boundary inputs, atomic write `.flush()`/`.sync_all()`, write failing regression tests (red), apply fixes. |
| **`bug-hunter-architect-rust`** | Smells 1-6 & Trait Centralization | Analyze recurring defect patterns, cluster code smells, and design lean Rust traits with formal contracts. |
| **`bug-hunter-mutator-rust`** | Mutation Testing & Coverage | Run `cargo-mutants`, find survived mutant branches, and write boundary unit tests ensuring assertions fail when code is mutated. |

- **Failing Scenario**: Concrete payload, CLI command, or input state that triggers the defect.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared resolver for the native and WASM Callisto setup actions.  This file
# deliberately contains the closed product-release vocabulary; it never reads
# a checkout manifest to decide what product or target to install.

set -euo pipefail

CALLISTO_REPOSITORY="orin-dx/callisto"
CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL="https://github.com/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/download"
CALLISTO_LATEST_API="https://api.github.com/repos/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest"

callisto_error() {
  printf '::error::setup-callisto: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  return 1
}

callisto_parse_version() {
  local requested="$1"
  case "$requested" in
    latest)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="latest"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION=""
      ;;
    callisto@*)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="${requested#callisto@}"
      ;;
    *)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="$requested"
      ;;
  esac

  if [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" \
    && ! "$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "version '$requested' must be latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_resolve_latest() {
  local tag
  if [[ -n "${CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG:-}" ]]; then
    tag="$CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG"
  else
    tag="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error --location "$CALLISTO_LATEST_API" | jq -er '.tag_name')" \
      || {
        callisto_error "could not resolve latest Callisto product release"
        return 1
      }
  fi

  case "$tag" in
    callisto@*) CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="${tag#callisto@}" ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' is not a callisto@X.Y.Z product release"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  if ! [[ "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' does not contain a semantic version"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_select_target() {
  local artifact="$1"
  if [[ "$artifact" == "wasm" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_TARGET="wasm32-wasip1"
    CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-moon-wasm32-wasip1.wasm"
    return 0
  fi

  local os_name arch_name
  os_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_OS:-$(uname -s)}"
  arch_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}"
  os_name="$(printf '%s' "$os_name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  case "${os_name}:${arch_name}" in
    darwin:arm64|darwin:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-apple-darwin"
      ;;
    linux:x86_64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    linux:arm64|linux:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "unsupported host ${os_name}/${arch_name}; supported native targets are aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-${CALLISTO_TARGET}.tar.gz"
}

# Resolve one immutable product release before source selection or cache use.
# Sets globals consumed by the composite actions and emits no network effects
# for exact input versions.
callisto_resolve() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" artifact="$3"
  case "$source" in auto|release|registry|local) ;; *)
    callisto_error "source '$source' must be auto, release, registry, or local"
    return 1
  esac
  callisto_parse_version "$version" || return 1
  if [[ "$source" == "local" && "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" ]]; then
    callisto_error "source=local only accepts version=latest; it cannot build an exact released version"
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ "$source" == "local" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="local"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG=""
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION=""
  elif [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "latest" ]]; then
    callisto_resolve_latest || return 1
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  else
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  fi

  CALLISTO_SOURCE="$source"
  callisto_select_target "$artifact" || return 1
  printf 'Resolved Callisto version: %s (target: %s)\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
}

callisto_write_outputs() {
  : "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set before writing resolver outputs}"
  {
    printf 'resolved-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
    printf 'release-tag=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG"
    printf 'registry-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION"
    printf 'source=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    printf 'target=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
    printf 'asset-name=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME"
  } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
}

callisto_require_local_workspace() {
  local workspace="$1"
  if [[ -f "$workspace/Cargo.toml" ]] \
    && rg -q '^name = "callisto-cli"' "$workspace/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml"; then
    return 0
  fi
  callisto_error "source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout"
}

callisto_install_native() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" tag="$3" asset="$4" bin_dir="$5" workspace="$6"
  mkdir -p "$bin_dir"
  case "$source" in
    local)
      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1
      local commit built_version
      commit="$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse HEAD)" || {
        callisto_error "source=local checkout has no readable commit"
        return 1
      }
      cargo build --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli
      cp "$workspace/target/debug/callisto" "$bin_dir/callisto"
      built_version="$("$bin_dir/callisto" --version)" || {
        callisto_error "locally built Callisto did not run"
        return 1
      }
      printf 'Built Callisto from checkout commit %s: %s\n' "$commit" "$built_version"
      ;;
    registry)
      cargo install callisto-cli --version "$version" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
      cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$bin_dir/callisto"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      # S-003 supplies the fail-closed 404-only auto fallback classification.
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" \
        --output "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}"
      tar -xzf "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}" -C "$bin_dir"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}

callisto_install_wasm() {
  local source="$1" tag="$2" asset="$3" destination="$4" workspace="$5"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
  case "$source" in
    local)
      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1
      cargo build --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-moon --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk --release
      cp "$workspace/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/callisto_moon.wasm" "$destination"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" --output "$destination"
      ;;
    registry)
      callisto_error "source=registry does not provide the callisto-moon WASM artifact"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Table-driven, no-network contract tests for the shared setup-action resolver.
set -u

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
# shellcheck source=../lib/setup-callisto.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/setup-callisto.sh"

fail=0

expect_resolve() {
  local name="$1" source_name="$2" version="$3" artifact="$4" os_name="$5" arch_name="$6" expected="$7"
  local output code
  output="$(CALLISTO_TEST_OS="$os_name" CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH="$arch_name" CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG="callisto@9.8.7" \
    callisto_resolve "$source_name" "$version" "$artifact" 2>&1)"
  code=$?
  if [[ $code -ne 0 || "$output" != *"$expected"* ]]; then
    printf 'FAIL %s: code=%s output=%s\n' "$name" "$code" "$output"
    fail=1
  else
    printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"
  fi
}

expect_reject() {
  local name="$1" source_name="$2" version="$3" artifact="$4" os_name="$5" arch_name="$6" expected="$7"
  local output code
  set +e
  output="$(CALLISTO_TEST_OS="$os_name" CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH="$arch_name" CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG="callisto@9.8.7" \
    callisto_resolve "$source_name" "$version" "$artifact" 2>&1)"
  code=$?
  set -e
  if [[ $code -eq 0 || "$output" != *"$expected"* ]]; then
    printf 'FAIL %s: code=%s output=%s\n' "$name" "$code" "$output"
    fail=1
  else
    printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"
  fi
}

# Every source mode and both exact spellings resolve to the same semantic
# version; latest is pinned by one injected release lookup before target use.
expect_resolve auto_exact auto 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 1.2.3'
expect_resolve release_product_tag release callisto@1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 1.2.3'
expect_resolve registry_exact registry 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 1.2.3'
expect_resolve local_latest local latest native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: local'
expect_resolve latest_pinned auto latest native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 9.8.7'

# The resolver exposes a single immutable latest result to action cache keys.
outputs_file="$(mktemp)"
# The resolver uses these dynamically-scoped variables after sourcing.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$outputs_file"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
CALLISTO_TEST_OS=Linux
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH=x86_64
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG=callisto@9.8.7
callisto_resolve auto latest wasm >/dev/null
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$outputs_file" callisto_write_outputs
if ! rg -Fx 'resolved-version=9.8.7' "$outputs_file" >/dev/null \
  || ! rg -Fx 'target=wasm32-wasip1' "$outputs_file" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL latest_writes_immutable_output\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS latest_writes_immutable_output\n'
fi
rm -f "$outputs_file"

# Native product target mapping is closed, while the WASM target is independent
# of the host running the resolver.
expect_resolve macos_arm64 auto 1.2.3 native Darwin arm64 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
expect_resolve linux_x86_64 auto 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
expect_resolve linux_aarch64 auto 1.2.3 native Linux aarch64 'aarch64-unknown-linux-musl'
expect_resolve wasm_target auto 1.2.3 wasm SunOS sun4u 'wasm32-wasip1'

expect_reject bad_source git 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'must be auto, release, registry, or local'
expect_reject bad_version auto callisto-cli@1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'must be latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z'
expect_reject local_exact local 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'source=local only accepts version=latest'
expect_reject macos_x86_64 auto 1.2.3 native Darwin x86_64 'unsupported host darwin/x86_64'
expect_reject linux_i686 auto 1.2.3 native Linux i686 'unsupported host linux/i686'
expect_reject windows auto 1.2.3 native Windows_NT x86_64 'unsupported host windows_nt/x86_64'

# A deliberate malformed latest response must not turn a branch-like tag into
# a cache or installation identity.
set +e
invalid_latest_output="$(CALLISTO_TEST_OS=Linux CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH=x86_64 CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG=main \
  callisto_resolve auto latest native 2>&1)"
invalid_latest_code=$?
set -e
if [[ $invalid_latest_code -eq 0 || "$invalid_latest_output" != *'not a callisto@X.Y.Z product release'* ]]; then
  printf 'FAIL latest_branch_tag_is_rejected: code=%s output=%s\n' "$invalid_latest_code" "$invalid_latest_output"
  fail=1

  printf 'PASS latest_branch_tag_is_rejected\n'
fi

wasm_dest="$(mktemp)"
rm -f "$wasm_dest"
set +e
wasm_registry_output="$(callisto_install_wasm registry callisto@1.2.3 ignored "$wasm_dest" /no-workspace 2>&1)"
wasm_registry_code=$?
set -e
if [[ $wasm_registry_code -eq 0 || "$wasm_registry_output" != *'source=registry does not provide'* ]]; then
  printf 'FAIL wasm_registry_is_rejected: code=%s output=%s\n' "$wasm_registry_code" "$wasm_registry_output"
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS wasm_registry_is_rejected\n'
fi
rm -f "$wasm_dest"

# Command stubs prove the registry branch is version-pinned and no resolver or
# installer branch can reach an unpinned cargo --git install.
calls_file="$(mktemp)"
stub_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$stub_dir/bin" "$stub_dir/workspace"
# This quoted program is intentionally written for the temporary command stub.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "cargo %%s\\n" "$*" >> %q\nmkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin"\ntouch "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto"\n' "$calls_file" > "$stub_dir/cargo"
chmod +x "$stub_dir/cargo"
PATH="$stub_dir:$PATH" RUNNER_TEMP="$stub_dir" \
  callisto_install_native registry 1.2.3 callisto@1.2.3 ignored "$stub_dir/bin" "$stub_dir/workspace"

  || rg -F -- '--git' "$calls_file" >/dev/null \
  || rg -n -- 'cargo install --git' "$ROOT/../setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml" "$ROOT/action.yml" "$ROOT/lib/setup-callisto.sh" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL pinned_registry_install_without_git_fallback\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS pinned_registry_install_without_git_fallback\n'
fi

# Even in a Callisto checkout, source=auto stays on the immutable release
# path; only source=local may build the checkout.
auto_calls="$(mktemp)"
# The helper invokes these command stubs indirectly.
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
curl() { printf 'curl %s\n' "$*" >> "$auto_calls"; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
tar() { printf 'tar %s\n' "$*" >> "$auto_calls"; }
CALLISTO_WORKSPACE="$(cd "$ROOT/../../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER_TEMP="$stub_dir" callisto_install_native auto 1.2.3 callisto@1.2.3 callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz "$stub_dir/bin" "$CALLISTO_WORKSPACE"
unset -f curl tar
if ! rg -F 'releases/download/callisto@1.2.3/callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz' "$auto_calls" >/dev/null \
  || rg -F 'cargo build' "$auto_calls" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL auto_does_not_build_monorepo_checkout\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS auto_does_not_build_monorepo_checkout\n'
fi
rm -f "$auto_calls"
rm -rf "$stub_dir" "$calls_file"

exit "$fail"
name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, Moon, and an immutable Callisto CLI release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        targets: wasm32-wasip1
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install Moon
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release
      id: resolve-callisto
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      run: |
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_resolve "$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE" "$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION" native
        callisto_write_outputs

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        RESOLVED_SOURCE: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.source }}
        RESOLVED_VERSION: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.registry-version }}
        RESOLVED_TAG: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.release-tag }}
        RESOLVED_ASSET: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.asset-name }}
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
        CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_install_native "$RESOLVED_SOURCE" "$RESOLVED_VERSION" "$RESOLVED_TAG" "$RESOLVED_ASSET" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
          echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
        fi
name: 'Setup Callisto WASM'
description: 'Downloads and caches an immutable callisto-moon.wasm product release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  dest:
    description: 'Destination path for callisto-moon.wasm'
    required: false
    default: '.moon/cache/ext/callisto-moon.wasm'

outputs:
  path:
    description: 'Path to the local cached callisto-moon.wasm file'
    value: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.destination }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release
      id: resolve-callisto
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_WASM_DEST: ${{ inputs.dest }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared resolver for the native and WASM Callisto setup actions.  This file
# deliberately contains the closed product-release vocabulary; it never reads
# a checkout manifest to decide what product or target to install.

set -euo pipefail

CALLISTO_REPOSITORY="orin-dx/callisto"
CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL="https://github.com/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/download"
CALLISTO_LATEST_API="https://api.github.com/repos/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest"

callisto_error() {
  printf '::error::setup-callisto: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  return 1
}

callisto_parse_version() {
  local requested="$1"
  case "$requested" in
    latest)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="latest"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION=""
      ;;
    callisto@*)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="${requested#callisto@}"
      ;;
    *)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="$requested"
      ;;
  esac

  if [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" \
    && ! "$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "version '$requested' must be latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_resolve_latest() {
  local tag
  if [[ -n "${CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG:-}" ]]; then
    tag="$CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG"
  else
    tag="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error --location "$CALLISTO_LATEST_API" | jq -er '.tag_name')" \
      || {
        callisto_error "could not resolve latest Callisto product release"
        return 1
      }
  fi

  case "$tag" in
    callisto@*) CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="${tag#callisto@}" ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' is not a callisto@X.Y.Z product release"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  if ! [[ "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' does not contain a semantic version"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_select_target() {
  local artifact="$1"
  if [[ "$artifact" == "wasm" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_TARGET="wasm32-wasip1"
    CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-moon-wasm32-wasip1.wasm"
    return 0
  fi

  local os_name arch_name
  os_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_OS:-$(uname -s)}"
  arch_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}"
  os_name="$(printf '%s' "$os_name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  case "${os_name}:${arch_name}" in
    darwin:arm64|darwin:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-apple-darwin"
      ;;
    linux:x86_64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    linux:arm64|linux:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "unsupported host ${os_name}/${arch_name}; supported native targets are aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-${CALLISTO_TARGET}.tar.gz"
}

# Resolve one immutable product release before source selection or cache use.
# Sets globals consumed by the composite actions and emits no network effects
# for exact input versions.
callisto_resolve() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" artifact="$3"
  case "$source" in auto|release|registry|local) ;; *)
    callisto_error "source '$source' must be auto, release, registry, or local"
    return 1
  esac
  callisto_parse_version "$version" || return 1
  if [[ "$source" == "local" && "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" ]]; then
    callisto_error "source=local only accepts version=latest; it cannot build an exact released version"
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ "$source" == "local" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="local"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG=""
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION=""
  elif [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "latest" ]]; then
    callisto_resolve_latest || return 1
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  else
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  fi

  CALLISTO_SOURCE="$source"
  callisto_select_target "$artifact" || return 1
  printf 'Resolved Callisto version: %s (target: %s)\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
}

callisto_write_outputs() {
  : "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set before writing resolver outputs}"

    printf 'registry-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION"
    printf 'source=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    printf 'target=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
    printf 'asset-name=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME"

}

  local workspace="$1"

      ;;
    release|auto)
      # S-003 supplies the fail-closed 404-only auto fallback classification.
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \

        --output "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}"
      tar -xzf "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}" -C "$bin_dir"

  esac
}

callisto_install_wasm() {
  local source="$1" tag="$2" asset="$3" destination="$4" workspace="$5"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"

      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1

      cp "$workspace/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/callisto_moon.wasm" "$destination"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" --output "$destination"
      ;;
    registry)
      callisto_error "source=registry does not provide the callisto-moon WASM artifact"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}

name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, Moon, and an immutable Callisto CLI release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        targets: wasm32-wasip1
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install Moon
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release
      id: resolve-callisto
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      run: |
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_resolve "$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE" "$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION" native
        callisto_write_outputs

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        RESOLVED_SOURCE: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.source }}
        RESOLVED_VERSION: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.registry-version }}
        RESOLVED_TAG: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.release-tag }}
        RESOLVED_ASSET: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.asset-name }}
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
        CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_install_native "$RESOLVED_SOURCE" "$RESOLVED_VERSION" "$RESOLVED_TAG" "$RESOLVED_ASSET" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
          echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
        fi
name: 'Setup Callisto WASM'
description: 'Downloads and caches an immutable callisto-moon.wasm product release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  dest:
    description: 'Destination path for callisto-moon.wasm'
    required: false

outputs:

runs:

    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared resolver for the native and WASM Callisto setup actions.  This file
# deliberately contains the closed product-release vocabulary; it never reads
# a checkout manifest to decide what product or target to install.

set -euo pipefail

CALLISTO_REPOSITORY="orin-dx/callisto"
CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL="https://github.com/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/download"
CALLISTO_LATEST_API="https://api.github.com/repos/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest"

callisto_error() {
  printf '::error::setup-callisto: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  return 1
}

callisto_parse_version() {
  local requested="$1"
  case "$requested" in
    latest)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="latest"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION=""
      ;;
    callisto@*)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="${requested#callisto@}"
      ;;
    *)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="$requested"
      ;;
  esac

  if [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" \
    && ! "$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "version '$requested' must be latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_resolve_latest() {
  local tag
  if [[ -n "${CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG:-}" ]]; then
    tag="$CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG"
  else
    tag="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error --location "$CALLISTO_LATEST_API" | jq -er '.tag_name')" \
      || {
        callisto_error "could not resolve latest Callisto product release"
        return 1
      }
  fi

  case "$tag" in
    callisto@*) CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="${tag#callisto@}" ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' is not a callisto@X.Y.Z product release"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  if ! [[ "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' does not contain a semantic version"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_select_target() {
  local artifact="$1"
  if [[ "$artifact" == "wasm" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_TARGET="wasm32-wasip1"
    CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-moon-wasm32-wasip1.wasm"
    return 0
  fi

  local os_name arch_name
  os_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_OS:-$(uname -s)}"
  arch_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}"
  os_name="$(printf '%s' "$os_name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  case "${os_name}:${arch_name}" in
    darwin:arm64|darwin:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-apple-darwin"
      ;;
    linux:x86_64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    linux:arm64|linux:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "unsupported host ${os_name}/${arch_name}; supported native targets are aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-${CALLISTO_TARGET}.tar.gz"
}

# Resolve one immutable product release before source selection or cache use.
# Sets globals consumed by the composite actions and emits no network effects
# for exact input versions.
callisto_resolve() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" artifact="$3"
  case "$source" in auto|release|registry|local) ;; *)
    callisto_error "source '$source' must be auto, release, registry, or local"
    return 1
  esac
  callisto_parse_version "$version" || return 1
  if [[ "$source" == "local" && "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" ]]; then
    callisto_error "source=local only accepts version=latest; it cannot build an exact released version"
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ "$source" == "local" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="local"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG=""
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION=""
  elif [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "latest" ]]; then
    callisto_resolve_latest || return 1
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  else
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  fi

  CALLISTO_SOURCE="$source"
  callisto_select_target "$artifact" || return 1
  printf 'Resolved Callisto version: %s (target: %s)\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
}

callisto_write_outputs() {
  : "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set before writing resolver outputs}"
  {
    printf 'resolved-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
    printf 'release-tag=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG"
    printf 'registry-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION"
    printf 'source=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    printf 'target=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
    printf 'asset-name=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME"
  } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
}

callisto_require_local_workspace() {
  local workspace="$1"
  if [[ -f "$workspace/Cargo.toml" ]] \
    && rg -q '^name = "callisto-cli"' "$workspace/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml"; then
    return 0
  fi
  callisto_error "source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout"
}

callisto_install_native() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" tag="$3" asset="$4" bin_dir="$5" workspace="$6"
  mkdir -p "$bin_dir"
  case "$source" in
    local)
      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1
      local commit built_version
      commit="$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse HEAD)" || {
        callisto_error "source=local checkout has no readable commit"
        return 1
      }
      cargo build --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli
      cp "$workspace/target/debug/callisto" "$bin_dir/callisto"
      built_version="$("$bin_dir/callisto" --version)" || {
        callisto_error "locally built Callisto did not run"
        return 1
      }
      printf 'Built Callisto from checkout commit %s: %s\n' "$commit" "$built_version"
      ;;
    registry)
      cargo install callisto-cli --version "$version" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
      cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$bin_dir/callisto"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      # S-003 supplies the fail-closed 404-only auto fallback classification.
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" \
        --output "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}"
      tar -xzf "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}" -C "$bin_dir"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}

callisto_install_wasm() {
  local source="$1" tag="$2" asset="$3" destination="$4" workspace="$5"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
  case "$source" in
    local)
      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1
      cargo build --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-moon --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk --release
      cp "$workspace/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/callisto_moon.wasm" "$destination"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" --output "$destination"
      ;;
    registry)
      callisto_error "source=registry does not provide the callisto-moon WASM artifact"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared resolver for the native and WASM Callisto setup actions.  This file
# deliberately contains the closed product-release vocabulary; it never reads
# a checkout manifest to decide what product or target to install.

set -euo pipefail

CALLISTO_REPOSITORY="orin-dx/callisto"
CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL="https://github.com/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/download"
CALLISTO_LATEST_API="https://api.github.com/repos/${CALLISTO_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest"

callisto_error() {
  printf '::error::setup-callisto: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  return 1
}

callisto_parse_version() {
  local requested="$1"
  case "$requested" in
    latest)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="latest"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION=""
      ;;
    callisto@*)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="${requested#callisto@}"
      ;;
    *)
      CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND="exact"
      CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION="$requested"
      ;;
  esac

  if [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" \
    && ! "$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "version '$requested' must be latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_resolve_latest() {
  local tag
  if [[ -n "${CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG:-}" ]]; then
    tag="$CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG"
  else
    tag="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error --location "$CALLISTO_LATEST_API" | jq -er '.tag_name')" \
      || {
        callisto_error "could not resolve latest Callisto product release"
        return 1
      }
  fi

  case "$tag" in
    callisto@*) CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="${tag#callisto@}" ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' is not a callisto@X.Y.Z product release"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  if ! [[ "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    callisto_error "latest release tag '$tag' does not contain a semantic version"
    return 1
  fi
}

callisto_select_target() {
  local artifact="$1"
  if [[ "$artifact" == "wasm" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_TARGET="wasm32-wasip1"
    CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-moon-wasm32-wasip1.wasm"
    return 0
  fi

  local os_name arch_name
  os_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_OS:-$(uname -s)}"
  arch_name="${CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH:-$(uname -m)}"
  os_name="$(printf '%s' "$os_name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  case "${os_name}:${arch_name}" in
    darwin:arm64|darwin:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-apple-darwin"
      ;;
    linux:x86_64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    linux:arm64|linux:aarch64)
      CALLISTO_TARGET="aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      ;;
    *)
      callisto_error "unsupported host ${os_name}/${arch_name}; supported native targets are aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME="callisto-${CALLISTO_TARGET}.tar.gz"
}

# Resolve one immutable product release before source selection or cache use.
# Sets globals consumed by the composite actions and emits no network effects
# for exact input versions.
callisto_resolve() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" artifact="$3"
  case "$source" in auto|release|registry|local) ;; *)
    callisto_error "source '$source' must be auto, release, registry, or local"
    return 1
  esac
  callisto_parse_version "$version" || return 1
  if [[ "$source" == "local" && "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "exact" ]]; then
    callisto_error "source=local only accepts version=latest; it cannot build an exact released version"
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ "$source" == "local" ]]; then
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="local"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG=""
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION=""
  elif [[ "$CALLISTO_REQUEST_KIND" == "latest" ]]; then
    callisto_resolve_latest || return 1
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  else
    CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION="$CALLISTO_REQUESTED_VERSION"
    CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG="callisto@${CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION}"
    CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION="$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
  fi

  CALLISTO_SOURCE="$source"
  callisto_select_target "$artifact" || return 1
  printf 'Resolved Callisto version: %s (target: %s)\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION" "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
}

callisto_write_outputs() {
  : "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set before writing resolver outputs}"
  {
    printf 'resolved-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_RESOLVED_VERSION"
    printf 'release-tag=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_RELEASE_TAG"
    printf 'registry-version=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_REGISTRY_VERSION"
    printf 'source=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    printf 'target=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_TARGET"
    printf 'asset-name=%s\n' "$CALLISTO_ASSET_NAME"
  } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
}

callisto_require_local_workspace() {
  local workspace="$1"
  if [[ -f "$workspace/Cargo.toml" ]] \
    && rg -q '^name = "callisto-cli"' "$workspace/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml"; then
    return 0
  fi
  callisto_error "source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout"
}

callisto_install_native() {
  local source="$1" version="$2" tag="$3" asset="$4" bin_dir="$5" workspace="$6"
  mkdir -p "$bin_dir"
  case "$source" in
    local)
      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1
      local commit built_version
      commit="$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse HEAD)" || {
        callisto_error "source=local checkout has no readable commit"
        return 1
      }
      cargo build --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli
      cp "$workspace/target/debug/callisto" "$bin_dir/callisto"
      built_version="$("$bin_dir/callisto" --version)" || {
        callisto_error "locally built Callisto did not run"
        return 1
      }
      printf 'Built Callisto from checkout commit %s: %s\n' "$commit" "$built_version"
      ;;
    registry)
      cargo install callisto-cli --version "$version" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
      cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$bin_dir/callisto"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      # S-003 supplies the fail-closed 404-only auto fallback classification.
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" \
        --output "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}"
      tar -xzf "${RUNNER_TEMP}/${asset}" -C "$bin_dir"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}

callisto_install_wasm() {
  local source="$1" tag="$2" asset="$3" destination="$4" workspace="$5"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
  case "$source" in
    local)
      callisto_require_local_workspace "$workspace" || return 1
      cargo build --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-moon --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk --release
      cp "$workspace/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/callisto_moon.wasm" "$destination"
      ;;
    release|auto)
      curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
        "${CALLISTO_RELEASES_URL}/${tag}/${asset}" --output "$destination"
      ;;
    registry)
      callisto_error "source=registry does not provide the callisto-moon WASM artifact"
      ;;
    *) callisto_error "internal error: unsupported source '$source'" ;;
  esac
}

  callisto_install_native registry 1.2.3 callisto@1.2.3 ignored "$stub_dir/bin" "$stub_dir/workspace"
if ! rg -F 'cargo install callisto-cli --version 1.2.3 --locked' "$calls_file" >/dev/null \
  || rg -F -- '--git' "$calls_file" >/dev/null \
  || rg -n -- 'cargo install --git' "$ROOT/../setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml" "$ROOT/action.yml" "$ROOT/lib/setup-callisto.sh" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL pinned_registry_install_without_git_fallback\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS pinned_registry_install_without_git_fallback\n'
fi

# Even in a Callisto checkout, source=auto stays on the immutable release
# path; only source=local may build the checkout.
auto_calls="$(mktemp)"

# shellcheck disable=SC2329
curl() { printf 'curl %s\n' "$*" >> "$auto_calls"; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
tar() { printf 'tar %s\n' "$*" >> "$auto_calls"; }
CALLISTO_WORKSPACE="$(cd "$ROOT/../../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER_TEMP="$stub_dir" callisto_install_native auto 1.2.3 callisto@1.2.3 callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz "$stub_dir/bin" "$CALLISTO_WORKSPACE"
unset -f curl tar
if ! rg -F 'releases/download/callisto@1.2.3/callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz' "$auto_calls" >/dev/null \
  || rg -F 'cargo build' "$auto_calls" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL auto_does_not_build_monorepo_checkout\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS auto_does_not_build_monorepo_checkout\n'
fi
rm -f "$auto_calls"
rm -rf "$stub_dir" "$calls_file"

exit "$fail"
name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, Moon, and an immutable Callisto CLI release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        targets: wasm32-wasip1
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install Moon
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release
      id: resolve-callisto
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      run: |
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_resolve "$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE" "$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION" native
        callisto_write_outputs

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        RESOLVED_SOURCE: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.source }}
        RESOLVED_VERSION: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.registry-version }}
        RESOLVED_TAG: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.release-tag }}
        RESOLVED_ASSET: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.asset-name }}
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
        CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_install_native "$RESOLVED_SOURCE" "$RESOLVED_VERSION" "$RESOLVED_TAG" "$RESOLVED_ASSET" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
          echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
        fi
name: 'Setup Callisto WASM'
description: 'Downloads and caches an immutable callisto-moon.wasm product release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  dest:
    description: 'Destination path for callisto-moon.wasm'
    required: false
    default: '.moon/cache/ext/callisto-moon.wasm'

outputs:
  path:
    description: 'Path to the local cached callisto-moon.wasm file'
    value: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.destination }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release
      id: resolve-callisto
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_WASM_DEST: ${{ inputs.dest }}
      run: |
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/../setup-callisto/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_resolve "$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE" "$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION" wasm
        callisto_write_outputs
        echo "destination=$INPUT_WASM_DEST" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Cache Callisto WASM
      id: cache-wasm
      # actions/cache v4.2.3
      uses: actions/cache@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684
      with:
        path: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.destination }}
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-callisto-wasm-${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.resolved-version }}

    - name: Download Callisto WASM Plugin
      id: download-wasm
      if: steps.cache-wasm.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
      shell: bash
      env:
        RESOLVED_DEST: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.destination }}
        RESOLVED_SOURCE: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.source }}
        RESOLVED_TAG: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.release-tag }}
        RESOLVED_ASSET: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.asset-name }}
      run: |
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/../setup-callisto/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_install_wasm "$RESOLVED_SOURCE" "$RESOLVED_TAG" "$RESOLVED_ASSET" "$RESOLVED_DEST" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "path=$RESOLVED_DEST" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

item.stdout:
# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci-fast

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
    cargo test --doc --all-features

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --all-features

# Exercise the Release-PR action's real shell block with Git and GitHub API
# boundaries faked. This proves the script's control flow given a decision
# shape; it does not call the real `callisto` binary, so it cannot catch a
# mismatch between what Callisto actually serializes and what this script's
# jq expressions expect. See test-release-action-binary for that check.
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Exercise the shared setup-action resolver without network or package-manager effects.
test-setup-actions:
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_resolver.sh

# CI variant of `test`: emits Nextest's JUnit report under target/nextest/ci
# for the trusted PR reporter. Keep the everyday local command artifact-free.
test-ci:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci
    cargo test --doc --all-features

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory & license check via moon / cargo-deny
audit:
    moon run :audit

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Verify Moon WASM plugin cross-compilation target and build the real
# cdylib. The black-box Extism/wasmtime sandbox test (tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs)
# is NOT re-run here: `just test`'s workspace-wide nextest run already builds
# and executes it (moon_pdk_test_utils is an unconditional dev-dependency, not
# gated by the `pdk` feature), so running it again via `cargo test` here would
# be a third full execution of the same suite once `coverage` runs it a second
# time under instrumentation -- pure redundant runtime, not extra coverage.
wasm-check:
    rustup target add wasm32-wasip1 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo check -p callisto-moon --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk
    cargo rustc -p callisto-moon --lib --target wasm32-wasip1 --features pdk --crate-type cdylib

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov. `_pdk.rs`-suffixed files
# are excluded: they contain code that only executes inside a real
# wasm32-wasip1 Extism host (see e.g. crates/callisto-moon/src/runner_pdk.rs's
# module doc comment) -- black-box tested via tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs, but
# invisible to native coverage instrumentation by construction, not a real
# testing gap. Any file matching this naming convention is understood to
# document its own exclusion this way.
#
# Optional `threshold`: when set, fails if total line coverage drops below
# it (--fail-under-lines). The human-readable summary is always emitted
# before enforcing the threshold: LCOV output itself contains no aggregate
# percentage, and a failed CI gate must say what developers need to improve.
# Unset locally (informational only, matching ARCHITECTURE.md's "coverage
# Global tasks inherited by every project (all crates use the rust toolchain uniformly).
tasks:
  build:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["build", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  test:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["test", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "**/*.snap"
      - "**/*.trycmd"

  lint:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["clippy", "-p", "$project", "--all-targets", "--", "-D", "warnings"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  format:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["fmt", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  format-check:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["fmt", "-p", "$project", "--", "--check"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  audit:
    command: "cargo-deny"
    args: ["check", "advisories"]
    inputs:
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  publish:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["publish", "-p", "$project", "--no-verify"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"
# Configures all projects within the workspace to create a project graph.
# Accepts a list of globs, a mapping of projects to relative file paths,
# or both values.
projects: ["crates/*"]

# Configures the version control system (VCS). Also known as
# source code management (SCM).
vcs:
  defaultBranch: "main"
  provider: "github"
  hooks:
    pre-commit:
      - "just pre-commit"
    pre-push:
      - "just pre-push"
