#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test for a real production incident (2026-08-27): consumer CI
# (orin-dx/michi) failed to install callisto because setup-callisto's
# fallback chain never tried crates.io -- only a GitHub Release binary
# tarball (which has no assets attached to any release, always 404s) and
# `cargo install --git` (broken on main by an unrelated yanked dependency).
# callisto-cli@0.5.0 was already published and installable from crates.io
# the whole time. This proves the new crates.io fallback is actually tried,
# in the right order, with the right args, before the git-source fallback.
set -u
ACTION_YML="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/action.yml"

extract_snippet() {
  # Starts after the TAG_NAME="${{ inputs.version || 'latest' }}" line (raw
  # GitHub Actions expression syntax, not valid bash on its own) -- the
  # caller sets TAG_NAME directly instead. Uses explicit line numbers, not a
  # `fi`-pattern range, because the block contains a nested if/elif/fi (OS
  # detection) before the outer if/elif/elif/else/fi this test targets --
  # a pattern-based range would stop at the first (inner) `fi` it finds.
  local start end
  start=$(grep -n '# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries' "$ACTION_YML" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  end=$(grep -n 'CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> \$GITHUB_PATH' "$ACTION_YML" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  end=$((end - 1))
  sed -n "${start},${end}p" "$ACTION_YML"
}

run_case() {
  local version="$1"
  local curl_behavior="$2"    # "fail" or "succeed"
  local cargo_behavior="$3"   # "crates-io-succeeds" or "crates-io-fails"
  local calls_file tmp_script workdir
  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
  workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "curl() { echo \"curl \$*\" >> '${calls_file}'; [[ '${curl_behavior}' == fail ]] && return 1 || return 0; }"
    echo "tar() { return 0; }"
    echo "cargo() {"
    echo "  echo \"cargo \$*\" >> '${calls_file}'"
    echo "  if [[ \"\$1\" == install && \"\$*\" == *'callisto-cli'* && \"\$*\" != *'--git'* ]]; then"
    echo "    [[ '${cargo_behavior}' == crates-io-succeeds ]] && { mkdir -p \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin\"; touch \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto\"; return 0; } || return 1"
    echo "  fi"
    echo "  if [[ \"\$*\" == *'--git'* ]]; then"
    echo "    mkdir -p \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin\"; touch \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto\"; return 0"
    echo "  fi"
    echo "}"
    echo "cp() { command cp \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "mkdir() { command mkdir \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "grep() { command grep \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "uname() { [[ \"\$1\" == -s ]] && echo Linux || echo x86_64; }"
    echo "RUNNER_TEMP='${workdir}'"
    echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE='${workdir}/not-callisto'"
    echo "mkdir -p \"\$GITHUB_WORKSPACE\""
    echo "GITHUB_PATH='${workdir}/github_path'"
    echo "touch \"\$GITHUB_PATH\""
    echo "TAG_NAME='${version}'"
    echo "CALLISTO_BIN_DIR='${workdir}/callisto-bin'"
    echo "mkdir -p '${workdir}/callisto-bin'"
    extract_snippet
  } > "$tmp_script"
  bash "$tmp_script" 2>/dev/null
  local code=$?
  cat "$calls_file"
  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file"
  rm -rf "$workdir"
  return $code
}

fail=0

# crates.io install must be attempted (and succeed) before the git fallback,
# when the GH-release binary download fails and version="latest".
out=$(run_case "latest" "fail" "crates-io-succeeds")
if [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli --locked"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: crates.io install (latest) must be attempted, got: $out"; fail=1
elif [[ "$out" == *"--git"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: git fallback must not run when crates.io install succeeds, got: $out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS: crates.io install (latest) attempted, git fallback skipped"
fi

# An explicit "callisto-cli@0.5.0" version must strip to a bare "0.5.0" for
# `cargo install --version`.
out=$(run_case "callisto-cli@0.5.0" "fail" "crates-io-succeeds")
if [[ "$out" != *"--version 0.5.0"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: explicit version must strip the callisto-cli@ prefix, got: $out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS: explicit version tag strips to bare semver for --version"
fi

# When crates.io install also fails, the git-source fallback must still run
# (it isn't removed, just demoted to last resort).
out=$(run_case "latest" "fail" "crates-io-fails")
if [[ "$out" != *"--git"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: git fallback must still run when crates.io install fails too, got: $out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS: git fallback still runs when crates.io install fails"
fi

exit $fail
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test for the download/extraction format dispatch in action.yml
# (the ASSET_NAME-driven case statements added to fix the Windows .zip vs
# .tar.gz mismatch). Extracts the actual run-step body from action.yml by a
# real text anchor -- the "# Detect OS platform architecture" comment through
# the end of the file -- so this test always exercises the file's current
# real logic; it cannot silently drift from it.
#
# The step's very first three lines (CALLISTO_BIN_DIR assignment, mkdir, and
# TAG_NAME="${{ inputs.version || 'latest' }}") are GitHub Actions template
# expressions that only resolve when the workflow runner preprocesses them;
# taken verbatim as bash they are a syntax error ("bad substitution"). This
# test starts extraction just after that line and supplies CALLISTO_BIN_DIR /
# TAG_NAME itself, matching what the runner would have already substituted.
set -u
ACTION_YML="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/action.yml"

extract_snippet() {
  sed -n '/# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries/,$p' "$ACTION_YML"
}

# Runs the extracted snippet with uname/curl stubbed per test case, and
# tar/unzip/cargo/cp always stubbed to record invocations into calls_file.
# GITHUB_WORKSPACE points at an empty temp dir (no Cargo.toml present, so the
# local-monorepo-build branch is always skipped here) and RUNNER_TEMP /
# CALLISTO_BIN_DIR / GITHUB_PATH point at temp paths.
run_case() {
  local uname_s="$1"
  local uname_m="$2"
  local curl_exit="$3"
  local calls_file workspace runner_temp bin_dir github_path tmp_script
  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
  workspace="$(mktemp -d)"
  runner_temp="$(mktemp -d)"
  bin_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  github_path="$(mktemp)"
  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
  {
    printf 'uname() {\n'
    printf '  case "$1" in\n'
    printf '    -s) echo %q ;;\n' "$uname_s"
    printf '    -m) echo %q ;;\n' "$uname_m"
    printf '    *) command uname "$@" ;;\n'
    printf '  esac\n'
    printf '}\n'
    printf 'curl() { echo "$*" >> %q; return %q; }\n' "$calls_file" "$curl_exit"
    printf 'tar() { echo "tar $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'unzip() { echo "unzip $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'cargo() { echo "cargo $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'cp() { echo "cp $*" >> %q; return 0; }\n' "$calls_file"
    printf 'GITHUB_WORKSPACE=%q\n' "$workspace"
    printf 'RUNNER_TEMP=%q\n' "$runner_temp"
    printf 'CALLISTO_BIN_DIR=%q\n' "$bin_dir"
    printf 'GITHUB_PATH=%q\n' "$github_path"
    printf 'TAG_NAME="latest"\n'
    extract_snippet
  } > "$tmp_script"
  bash "$tmp_script"
  local code=$?
  echo "---CALLS---"
  cat "$calls_file"
  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file" "$github_path"
  rm -rf "$workspace" "$runner_temp" "$bin_dir"
  return $code
}

fail=0

# 1. Windows runner -> zip asset, curl destination is not the old hardcoded
# tar.gz path, unzip is invoked, tar is not.
out=$(run_case "MINGW64_NT-10.0" "x86_64" 0); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
  || [[ "$out" == *"-o "*"callisto.tar.gz"* ]] \
  || [[ "$out" != *"unzip -q "*" -d "* ]] \
  || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL test_windows_uses_zip_and_unzip: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS test_windows_uses_zip_and_unzip"
fi

# 2. macOS arm64 regression -> unchanged tar.gz behavior, unzip not invoked.
out=$(run_case "Darwin" "arm64" 0); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
  || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "* ]] \
  || [[ "$out" != *" -C "* ]] \
  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL test_macos_arm64_still_uses_targz: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS test_macos_arm64_still_uses_targz"
fi

# 3. Linux amd64 regression -> unchanged tar.gz behavior, unzip not invoked.
out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 0); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
  || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "* ]] \
  || [[ "$out" != *" -C "* ]] \
  || [[ "$out" == *"unzip"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL test_linux_amd64_still_uses_targz: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS test_linux_amd64_still_uses_targz"
fi

# 4. Unknown/exotic OS -> defensive catch-all fires (not an error): tar.gz
# fallback runs, step still exits 0.
out=$(run_case "SunOS" "sun4u" 0); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
  || [[ "$out" != *"tar -xzf "* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL test_unknown_os_falls_back_to_targz_no_error: code=$code out=$out"; fail=1
else
  echo "PASS test_unknown_os_falls_back_to_targz_no_error"
fi

# 5. Download failure -> falls through to the pre-existing cargo-install
# fallback chain untouched: neither tar nor unzip invoked, cargo install
# callisto-cli invoked, step still exits 0. Proves the new dispatch (which
# now runs unconditionally before the if/elif chain) has no side effect on
# that fallback.
out=$(run_case "Linux" "x86_64" 1); code=$?
if [[ $code -ne 0 ]] \
  || [[ "$out" == *"tar -xzf"* ]] \

else
  echo "PASS test_download_failure_falls_back_to_cargo_install"
fi

exit $fail

  local job="$1" next_job="$2"
  sed -n "/^  ${job}:$/,/^  ${next_job}:$/p" "$workflow"
}

require_line() {
  local block="$1" expected="$2" description="$3"
  if ! grep -Fqx "$expected" <<< "$block"; then
    printf 'release workflow contract failed: %s\n' "$description" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

require_line "$build" '      contents: read' 'build must read the intent-bound source tree'
require_line "$build" '      attestations: write' 'build must create provenance attestations'
require_line "$build" '      id-token: write' 'build must mint the Sigstore OIDC identity'
require_line "$build" '          include-hidden-files: true' 'build must upload .release-handoff -- upload-artifact drops dotfiles by default and "execute" would silently receive nothing'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test for a real production incident (2026-08-27): consumer CI
# (orin-dx/michi) failed to install callisto because setup-callisto's
# fallback chain never tried crates.io -- only a GitHub Release binary
# tarball (which has no assets attached to any release, always 404s) and
# `cargo install --git` (broken on main by an unrelated yanked dependency).
# callisto-cli@0.5.0 was already published and installable from crates.io
# the whole time. This proves the new crates.io fallback is actually tried,
# in the right order, with the right args, before the git-source fallback.
set -u
ACTION_YML="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/action.yml"

extract_snippet() {
  # Starts after the TAG_NAME="${{ inputs.version || 'latest' }}" line (raw
  # GitHub Actions expression syntax, not valid bash on its own) -- the
  # caller sets TAG_NAME directly instead. Uses explicit line numbers, not a
  # `fi`-pattern range, because the block contains a nested if/elif/fi (OS
  # detection) before the outer if/elif/elif/else/fi this test targets --
  # a pattern-based range would stop at the first (inner) `fi` it finds.
  local start end
  start=$(grep -n '# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries' "$ACTION_YML" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  end=$(grep -n 'CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> \$GITHUB_PATH' "$ACTION_YML" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  end=$((end - 1))
  sed -n "${start},${end}p" "$ACTION_YML"
}

run_case() {
  local version="$1"
  local curl_behavior="$2"    # "fail" or "succeed"
  local cargo_behavior="$3"   # "crates-io-succeeds" or "crates-io-fails"
  local calls_file tmp_script workdir
  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
  workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "curl() { echo \"curl \$*\" >> '${calls_file}'; [[ '${curl_behavior}' == fail ]] && return 1 || return 0; }"
    echo "tar() { return 0; }"
    echo "cargo() {"
    echo "  echo \"cargo \$*\" >> '${calls_file}'"
    echo "  if [[ \"\$1\" == install && \"\$*\" == *'callisto-cli'* && \"\$*\" != *'--git'* ]]; then"
    echo "    [[ '${cargo_behavior}' == crates-io-succeeds ]] && { mkdir -p \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin\"; touch \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto\"; return 0; } || return 1"
    echo "  fi"
    echo "  if [[ \"\$*\" == *'--git'* ]]; then"
    echo "    mkdir -p \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin\"; touch \"\${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto\"; return 0"
    echo "  fi"
    echo "}"
    echo "cp() { command cp \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "mkdir() { command mkdir \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "grep() { command grep \"\$@\"; }"
    echo "uname() { [[ \"\$1\" == -s ]] && echo Linux || echo x86_64; }"
    echo "RUNNER_TEMP='${workdir}'"
    echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE='${workdir}/not-callisto'"
    echo "mkdir -p \"\$GITHUB_WORKSPACE\""
    echo "GITHUB_PATH='${workdir}/github_path'"
    echo "touch \"\$GITHUB_PATH\""
    echo "TAG_NAME='${version}'"
    echo "CALLISTO_BIN_DIR='${workdir}/callisto-bin'"
    echo "mkdir -p '${workdir}/callisto-bin'"
    extract_snippet
  } > "$tmp_script"
  bash "$tmp_script" 2>/dev/null
  local code=$?
  cat "$calls_file"
  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file"
  rm -rf "$workdir"
  return $code
}

fail=0

# crates.io install must be attempted (and succeed) before the git fallback,
# when the GH-release binary download fails and version="latest".
out=$(run_case "latest" "fail" "crates-io-succeeds")
if [[ "$out" != *"cargo install callisto-cli --locked"* ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: crates.io install (latest) must be attempted, got: $out"; fail=1

  echo "FAIL: git fallback must not run when crates.io install succeeds, got: $out"; fail=1

  echo "PASS: crates.io install (latest) attempted, git fallback skipped"
fi

# An explicit "callisto-cli@0.5.0" version must strip to a bare "0.5.0" for
# `cargo install --version`.
out=$(run_case "callisto-cli@0.5.0" "fail" "crates-io-succeeds")

  echo "FAIL: explicit version must strip the callisto-cli@ prefix, got: $out"; fail=1

  echo "PASS: git fallback still runs when crates.io install fails"
fi

exit $fail

### [Medium] Local WASM cache can silently reuse another commit’s plugin

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: `.github/actions/setup-callisto/lib/setup-callisto.sh:112-114,189-192`; `.github/actions/setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml:44,48`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift / Staleness
- **Root Cause**: `source=local` always resolves to the constant version `local`. The WASM cache key therefore becomes `<os>-callisto-wasm-local`, while an exact cache hit skips `callisto_install_wasm`, including its local checkout build.
- **Failing Scenario**: Commit A runs the WASM action with `source=local` and populates the cache. Commit B uses the same input and OS; the cache hits, lines 189-192 never execute, and Commit A’s WASM is returned as though built from Commit B. This violates AC-003’s current-checkout semantics.
- **Verification Strategy**: Add a composite-control-flow fixture that seeds a `source=local` cache for commit A, invokes the action for commit B, and requires the build to run and output bytes/identity from B. Local mode should bypass the release cache or key it by checkout commit.

### Coverage gap

`test_resolver.sh:44-48,57-64,74-77,125,144` does not connect resolver outputs to installer inputs:

- It checks output substrings, but not `release-tag`, `registry-version`, or `asset-name`.
- Installer tests pass hard-coded tag/version/asset values.
- It does not execute composite cache-hit control flow, so the confirmed stale-local-cache defect passes.
- It does not exercise both exact-version spellings across every non-local source mode as AC-006 states.

A broken tag, registry version, or asset-name assignment could therefore leave `just test-setup-actions` green.

### Verified with no further finding

- Exact/latest parsing, supported and rejected platform mappings, explicit-local-only checkout builds, action environment wiring, and absence of unpinned `cargo install --git`.
- `just test-setup-actions`, `bash -n`, and `shellcheck` pass.
- `Cargo.lock` is minimal: only `rustls 0.23.45`, `chacha20 0.10.2`, and required `rustls` companions `aws-lc-rs 1.18.1`, `aws-lc-sys 0.45.0`, and `rustls-webpki 0.103.15` move. No manifest or `deny.toml` changes.
- Locked dependency trees contain only `rustls 0.23.45` and `chacha20 0.10.2`.
- Forced current-database `just audit` passed on 2026-09-16.
- Focused `moon run callisto-moon:test` passed, including all 13 real WASM sandbox tests.
- Full `just test` and `just wasm-check` are presently blocked by concurrent, out-of-scope Rust edits; their failures are in workspace-membership tests and incomplete `release.rs` symbols, not the lockfile transaction.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Table-driven, no-network contract tests for the shared setup-action resolver.
set -u

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
# shellcheck source=../lib/setup-callisto.sh
source "$ROOT/lib/setup-callisto.sh"

fail=0

assert_exact_handoff() {
  local name="$1" source_name="$2" requested_version="$3"
  local outputs_file stub_dir calls_file resolved_tag resolved_registry resolved_asset
  outputs_file="$(mktemp)"
  stub_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
  mkdir -p "$stub_dir/bin"

  GITHUB_OUTPUT="$outputs_file"
  CALLISTO_TEST_OS=Linux
  CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH=x86_64
  callisto_resolve "$source_name" "$requested_version" native >/dev/null
  callisto_write_outputs
  resolved_tag="$(rg '^release-tag=' "$outputs_file" | cut -d= -f2-)"
  resolved_registry="$(rg '^registry-version=' "$outputs_file" | cut -d= -f2-)"
  resolved_asset="$(rg '^asset-name=' "$outputs_file" | cut -d= -f2-)"

  # These command stubs record the installer boundary without external I/O.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2016
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "curl %%s\\n" "$*" >> %q\n' "$calls_file" > "$stub_dir/curl"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2016
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "tar %%s\\n" "$*" >> %q\n' "$calls_file" > "$stub_dir/tar"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2016
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "cargo %%s\\n" "$*" >> %q\nmkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin"\ntouch "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto"\n' "$calls_file" > "$stub_dir/cargo"
  chmod +x "$stub_dir/curl" "$stub_dir/tar" "$stub_dir/cargo"
  PATH="$stub_dir:$PATH" RUNNER_TEMP="$stub_dir" \
    callisto_install_native "$source_name" "$resolved_registry" "$resolved_tag" "$resolved_asset" "$stub_dir/bin" "$stub_dir/no-workspace"

  if [[ "$resolved_tag" != 'callisto@1.2.3' \
    || "$resolved_registry" != '1.2.3' \
    || "$resolved_asset" != 'callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz' ]]; then
    printf 'FAIL %s_resolver_outputs: tag=%s registry=%s asset=%s\n' "$name" "$resolved_tag" "$resolved_registry" "$resolved_asset"
    fail=1
  elif [[ "$source_name" == registry ]] \
    && ! rg -F 'cargo install callisto-cli --version 1.2.3 --locked' "$calls_file" >/dev/null; then
    printf 'FAIL %s_installer_handoff: expected pinned registry install\n' "$name"
    fail=1
  elif [[ "$source_name" != registry ]] \
    && ! rg -F "releases/download/callisto@1.2.3/${resolved_asset}" "$calls_file" >/dev/null; then
    printf 'FAIL %s_installer_handoff: expected exact release URL\n' "$name"
    fail=1
  else
    printf 'PASS %s_resolver_to_installer_handoff\n' "$name"
  fi
  rm -rf "$stub_dir" "$outputs_file" "$calls_file"
}

expect_resolve() {
  local name="$1" source_name="$2" version="$3" artifact="$4" os_name="$5" arch_name="$6" expected="$7"
  local output code
  output="$(CALLISTO_TEST_OS="$os_name" CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH="$arch_name" CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG="callisto@9.8.7" \
    callisto_resolve "$source_name" "$version" "$artifact" 2>&1)"
  code=$?
  if [[ $code -ne 0 || "$output" != *"$expected"* ]]; then
    printf 'FAIL %s: code=%s output=%s\n' "$name" "$code" "$output"
    fail=1
  else
    printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"
  fi
}

expect_reject() {
  local name="$1" source_name="$2" version="$3" artifact="$4" os_name="$5" arch_name="$6" expected="$7"
  local output code
  set +e
  output="$(CALLISTO_TEST_OS="$os_name" CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH="$arch_name" CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG="callisto@9.8.7" \
    callisto_resolve "$source_name" "$version" "$artifact" 2>&1)"
  code=$?
  set -e
  if [[ $code -eq 0 || "$output" != *"$expected"* ]]; then
    printf 'FAIL %s: code=%s output=%s\n' "$name" "$code" "$output"
    fail=1
  else
    printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name"
  fi
}

# Every source mode and both exact spellings resolve to the same semantic
# version; latest is pinned by one injected release lookup before target use.
expect_resolve auto_exact auto 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 1.2.3'
expect_resolve release_product_tag release callisto@1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 1.2.3'
expect_resolve registry_exact registry 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 1.2.3'
expect_resolve local_latest local latest native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: local'
expect_resolve latest_pinned auto latest native Linux x86_64 'Resolved Callisto version: 9.8.7'

# Every exact spelling passes the helper's canonical outputs directly to its
# installer; no action input is reused as a source identity after resolution.
assert_exact_handoff auto_bare auto 1.2.3
assert_exact_handoff auto_product_tag auto callisto@1.2.3
assert_exact_handoff release_bare release 1.2.3
assert_exact_handoff release_product_tag release callisto@1.2.3
assert_exact_handoff registry_bare registry 1.2.3
assert_exact_handoff registry_product_tag registry callisto@1.2.3

# The resolver exposes a single immutable latest result to action cache keys.
outputs_file="$(mktemp)"
# The resolver uses these dynamically-scoped variables after sourcing.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$outputs_file"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
CALLISTO_TEST_OS=Linux
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH=x86_64
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG=callisto@9.8.7
callisto_resolve auto latest wasm >/dev/null
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$outputs_file" callisto_write_outputs
if ! rg -Fx 'resolved-version=9.8.7' "$outputs_file" >/dev/null \
  || ! rg -Fx 'target=wasm32-wasip1' "$outputs_file" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL latest_writes_immutable_output\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS latest_writes_immutable_output\n'
fi
rm -f "$outputs_file"

# Native product target mapping is closed, while the WASM target is independent
# of the host running the resolver.
expect_resolve macos_arm64 auto 1.2.3 native Darwin arm64 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
expect_resolve linux_x86_64 auto 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
expect_resolve linux_aarch64 auto 1.2.3 native Linux aarch64 'aarch64-unknown-linux-musl'
expect_resolve wasm_target auto 1.2.3 wasm SunOS sun4u 'wasm32-wasip1'

expect_reject bad_source git 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'must be auto, release, registry, or local'
expect_reject bad_version auto callisto-cli@1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'must be latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z'
expect_reject local_exact local 1.2.3 native Linux x86_64 'source=local only accepts version=latest'
expect_reject macos_x86_64 auto 1.2.3 native Darwin x86_64 'unsupported host darwin/x86_64'
expect_reject linux_i686 auto 1.2.3 native Linux i686 'unsupported host linux/i686'
expect_reject windows auto 1.2.3 native Windows_NT x86_64 'unsupported host windows_nt/x86_64'

# A deliberate malformed latest response must not turn a branch-like tag into
# a cache or installation identity.
set +e
invalid_latest_output="$(CALLISTO_TEST_OS=Linux CALLISTO_TEST_ARCH=x86_64 CALLISTO_LATEST_TAG=main \
  callisto_resolve auto latest native 2>&1)"
invalid_latest_code=$?
set -e
if [[ $invalid_latest_code -eq 0 || "$invalid_latest_output" != *'not a callisto@X.Y.Z product release'* ]]; then
  printf 'FAIL latest_branch_tag_is_rejected: code=%s output=%s\n' "$invalid_latest_code" "$invalid_latest_output"
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS latest_branch_tag_is_rejected\n'
fi

# WASM is an explicit artifact-type divergence: it has no registry package.
wasm_dest="$(mktemp)"
rm -f "$wasm_dest"
set +e
wasm_registry_output="$(callisto_install_wasm registry callisto@1.2.3 ignored "$wasm_dest" /no-workspace 2>&1)"
wasm_registry_code=$?
set -e
if [[ $wasm_registry_code -eq 0 || "$wasm_registry_output" != *'source=registry does not provide'* ]]; then
  printf 'FAIL wasm_registry_is_rejected: code=%s output=%s\n' "$wasm_registry_code" "$wasm_registry_output"
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS wasm_registry_is_rejected\n'
fi
rm -f "$wasm_dest"

# Local WASM output represents an arbitrary checkout commit. The action must
# skip actions/cache so every local request reaches the current checkout build.
wasm_action="$ROOT/../setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml"
if ! rg -U -F $'id: cache-wasm\n      # A local build represents the checkout commit, not a reusable product\n      # release payload. Never restore another checkout\x27s plugin from cache.\n      if: steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.source != \'local\'' "$wasm_action" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL local_wasm_bypasses_cache\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS local_wasm_bypasses_cache\n'
fi

# Command stubs prove the registry branch is version-pinned and no resolver or
# installer branch can reach an unpinned cargo --git install.
calls_file="$(mktemp)"
stub_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$stub_dir/bin" "$stub_dir/workspace"
# This quoted program is intentionally written for the temporary command stub.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "cargo %%s\\n" "$*" >> %q\nmkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin"\ntouch "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto"\n' "$calls_file" > "$stub_dir/cargo"
chmod +x "$stub_dir/cargo"
PATH="$stub_dir:$PATH" RUNNER_TEMP="$stub_dir" \
  callisto_install_native registry 1.2.3 callisto@1.2.3 ignored "$stub_dir/bin" "$stub_dir/workspace"
if ! rg -F 'cargo install callisto-cli --version 1.2.3 --locked' "$calls_file" >/dev/null \
  || rg -F -- '--git' "$calls_file" >/dev/null \
  || rg -n -- 'cargo install --git' "$ROOT/../setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml" "$ROOT/action.yml" "$ROOT/lib/setup-callisto.sh" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL pinned_registry_install_without_git_fallback\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS pinned_registry_install_without_git_fallback\n'
fi

# Even in a Callisto checkout, source=auto stays on the immutable release
# path; only source=local may build the checkout.
auto_calls="$(mktemp)"
# The helper invokes these command stubs indirectly.
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
curl() { printf 'curl %s\n' "$*" >> "$auto_calls"; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
tar() { printf 'tar %s\n' "$*" >> "$auto_calls"; }
CALLISTO_WORKSPACE="$(cd "$ROOT/../../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER_TEMP="$stub_dir" callisto_install_native auto 1.2.3 callisto@1.2.3 callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz "$stub_dir/bin" "$CALLISTO_WORKSPACE"
unset -f curl tar
if ! rg -F 'releases/download/callisto@1.2.3/callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz' "$auto_calls" >/dev/null \
  || rg -F 'cargo build' "$auto_calls" >/dev/null; then
  printf 'FAIL auto_does_not_build_monorepo_checkout\n'
  fail=1
else
  printf 'PASS auto_does_not_build_monorepo_checkout\n'
fi
rm -f "$auto_calls"
rm -rf "$stub_dir" "$calls_file"

exit "$fail"
name: 'Setup Callisto WASM'
description: 'Downloads and caches an immutable callisto-moon.wasm product release'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto, release, registry, or local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Callisto version: latest, X.Y.Z, or callisto@X.Y.Z.'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  dest:
    description: 'Destination path for callisto-moon.wasm'
    required: false
    default: '.moon/cache/ext/callisto-moon.wasm'

outputs:
  path:
    description: 'Path to the local cached callisto-moon.wasm file'
    value: ${{ steps.resolve-callisto.outputs.destination }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Resolve immutable Callisto release
      id: resolve-callisto
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_WASM_DEST: ${{ inputs.dest }}
      run: |
        source "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/../setup-callisto/lib/setup-callisto.sh"
        callisto_resolve "$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE" "$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION" wasm
        callisto_write_outputs
